content.comment_body: Hello, We are facing a problem with [product_name] software, which prevents us from selecting the temperature sensor range of 0 to 50°C, and only permits ranges like 0 to 48°C. The system displays the message: “The measurement range determined by gain/offset is invalid. Used measurement range 0 to 48”. When adjusting the gain and offset parameters, we notice the minimum and maximum fixed range allowed is from 2 to 50°C. Please refer to the attached [document] with relevant screenshots. Could you provide some recommendations? Thank you.

Please upload your program as a ZIP file. Additionally, specify the exact physical measuring range your temperature signal at AI1 covers. Screenshots are helpful, though it is always better to have the actual program.
Is your sensor rated for 0–50°C and 0–10 Volt? Try using: Gain 0.05 and Offset 0. Create your program using the FBD (Function Block Diagram) method, not LD (Ladder Diagram).

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering limitations in configuring the desired temperature sensor range in [product_name] software, specifically being unable to set it precisely to 0–50°C. The software limits the configurable range to 0–48°C or 2–50°C depending on gain and offset adjustments, which complicates sensor calibration. Although the error message is clear, users remain uncertain about how to achieve the range they need.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to allow them to configure the calibration of their temperature sensors exactly to the desired 0–50°C range, without restrictions imposed by software validation on gain and offset settings.
